analysis: Test-only changes. CoordinatorClientTests.swift head 578-591 replaces sampled nextDelay() checks with deterministic nextDelayRange() assertions ([0.5...1,1...2,2...4,2...4], reset to 0.5...1); this implies a new or renamed ExponentialBackoff API in production source not supplied here. CoordinatorIntegrationTests.swift adds tests (head 456-491) asserting that a coordinator-side 1012 close reconnects within 0-1 s and that a session open past CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.stableSessionDuration resets the backoff. It also adds a reconnectPolicy parameter to makeClient/CoordinatorClient (head 652-653, 674-675) and helpers (677-726), and removes the release-workflow skip comment so the suite runs in scripts/run-provider-tests.sh. No changes to attestation, encryption, token or authorization logic are visible. Re-registration still regenerates attestation per connection (lines 70-90, unchanged), consistent with TB-009's ±2 min re-sign. Integration questions: the production CoordinatorClient change, not in this batch, must be checked to confirm three things. First, a 1012 fast-reconnect path cannot be abused by a malicious or compromised coordinator path or MITM into a tight reconnect loop. The coordinator is trusted, but jitter and a floor must remain to avoid a thundering herd or DoS (TB-002 availability). Second, the stable-session reset uses a monotonic clock. Third, the default stableSessionDuration (~60 s per comments) is preserved. Each reconnect must keep re-signing fresh attestation and must not reuse stale App Attest grants (T-053). The CI workflow change (release-swift.yml) is not supplied.
